 Most recent Most popular 'Who is this guy?' - Hart on reaction to Kane making England squad published at 19:26 GMT 19:26 GMT 
 England v Croatia (19:45 GMT) 
 Joe Hart 
Former England goalkeeper to BBC Sport 
 My reaction when he first came into the England squad was: 'Alright, who is this guy?
 Then I was like: 'Oh OK, he's good! Then he kept coming back [into the England squad] and my reaction was: 'Flipping heck, he's getting better!' 
 I went to Tottenham during Covid and it got to the point in training where he was that good that I wasn't even diving for his shots. I was thinking: 'I adore you, but you are frustrating the life out of me.'
 He's never particularly relied on pace. It's all about his thought process and his brain and how he calculates the game.

 'I dreamt of that moment being at Wembley' - Kane reflects on England debut published at 19:24 GMT 19:24 GMT 
 England v Croatia (19:45 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Harry Kane says scoring on his England debut is still "one of my favourite moments" as he is set to break his nation's appearance record.
 Reflecting on that night at Wembley, the England captain told BBC's football correspondent John Murray and senior football reporter Ian Dennis: "It is still fresh in the memory, but a lot has happened since obviously, a lot of good moments.
 "I just think the years go by so quickly, it’s pretty crazy, but what a special occasion it was. [It is] still one of my favourite moments of my career.
 "I think it's just a dream come true; I grew up wanting to play for England. I dreamt of that moment being at Wembley, coming on for someone like Wayne Rooney, scoring a goal within a couple of minutes.
 "It all just kind of fell into place at the right time. I just remember being excited to get onto the pitch, a little bit nervous, excited, all those emotions.
 "I remember how loud it was, that almost motivated me to do something special.
 "Before I know it, I am heading a ball into the back of the net, I am running off celebrating.
 "It was just like this whirlwind of all these emotions and then from that moment I just can’t really remember the last 20 minutes or however long it was that I played.
 "I don’t even know if I touched the ball after that.
 "It was so many emotions in such a short period of time; just as good as it gets really."

 Kane's top 10 England moments - which was your favourite? published at 19:21 GMT 19:21 GMT 
 England v Croatia (19:45 GMT) 
 What was your favourite Harry Kane moment? We've put together a list of 10 here and you can get in touch and let us know yours too.
 From goals to take England to major finals to match-winning moments that get the Three Lions out of a scrape, let us know your favourite.
 We haven't included Kane's post-Mexico interview at the World Cup as I think we can all agree, that is the best moment by a country mile.
 Here it is again because who wouldn't want to relive this moment.
 Media caption, 'I'm speechless' - Kane reacts to England's victory over Mexico

 England v Croatia (19:45 GMT) 
 Jude Bellingham has previously said his biggest dream would be to share the pitch with his brother playing for England - bigger than winning trophies or awards.
 Will Thomas Tuchel make that dream come true?

 Keeping it in the family published at 19:15 GMT 19:15 GMT 
 England v Croatia (19:45 GMT) 
 The Bellinghams will become the first brothers to play for England for 19 years if Jobe wins his first cap and appears alongside Jude, a veteran of 60 appearances, in the match against Croatia at Wembley tonight.
 What a moment that would be.
 I was just trying to think of other brothers who have played for England.
 The Nevilles, the Charltons - any others?

 Special night for Bellingham brothers published at 19:12 GMT 19:12 GMT 
 England v Croatia (19:45 GMT) 
 For the first time England boss Thomas Tuchel has called up both Jude Bellingham and his younger brother Jobe to the Three Lions squad.
 While Jude, 23, is establishing himself as a footballing great at European heavyweights Real Madrid following a spell at Borussia Dortmund, Jobe, 21, is continuing his football education at his brother's former club in Germany after two seasons with Sunderland.
 The brothers started out at boyhood club Birmingham City and played 70 league and cup games between them for the club after graduating from the academy.
 They have never appeared together in a senior match, however, as Jude - who joined Birmingham aged eight - had left by the time Jobe broke into the first team in 2022.
 That could all change tonight.
 Image source, Jude Bellingham Instagram

 Tuchel's evolving squad published at 19:09 GMT 19:09 GMT 
 England v Croatia (19:45 GMT) 
 Alex Howell 
BBC Sport England reporter at Wembley 
 Thomas Tuchel has played down expectations before England take on Croatia tonight. In his press conference he warned not to expect another 7-0 win like the one they produced in the last international window. 
 The Three Lions performed well in all four of their matches last time out in the Nations League and only lost narrowly to world champions Spain. 
 This England squad feels like it is continuing to evolve as Tuchel prepares for Euro 2028 and includes young players such as Josh King, Rio Ngumoha and Jobe Bellingham. 
 Jobe and King don't have caps yet and could make their debuts.

 Seven(th) heaven published at 19:06 GMT 19:06 GMT 
 England v Croatia (19:45 GMT) 
 When these two sides met in the Nations League in the last international break, England thrashed Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka with Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka each netting twice while Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers all scored one.
 When the two met at this summer's World Cup it was a closer encounter but England won the match 4-2 and many suggested the second half was the peak of the Three Lions' tournament in the United States.
 Could it be another thriller tonight?

 'Like a movie' - Kane on winning Ballon d'Or published at 18:54 GMT 18:54 GMT 
 England v Croatia (19:45 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Harry Kane said the moment he won the Ballon d'Or was "almost like a movie" as his name was read out by Brazil legend Ronaldo.
 Speaking to BBC's John Murray and Ian Dennis about winning the much-coveted award, Kane said: "I think I maybe underappreciated how big it was going to be, how big the reaction was going to be.
 "It’s just been crazy, whether it’s messages on my phone or on social media, or people calling me, and just being in the street and everyone congratulating me.
 "I think the actual moment when Ronaldo said my name, it’s strange, it's almost like a movie.
 "In the moment, it was like in slow motion and the confetti was supposed to fall and all this, but when I watched it back, I had my hand to my mouth and maybe a couple of seconds and I was out, but in the actual moment, it felt like I was doing it for a minute.
 "It was a really unique feeling because it is different to playing a game or scoring a goal, because it is so individual, it is nothing you can kind of do.
 "Your mind is playing games with you the whole night, whether it is going to be you or not.
 "So, when he actually said my name, it was just a crazy emotion."

 Post published at 18:51 GMT 18:51 GMT 
 England v Croatia (19:45 GMT) 
 Of course, with all this happening at Wembley tonight there will be celebrations before kick-off.
 Peter Shilton, who currently shares Harry Kane's record of 125 England caps, will be part of a pre-match presentation to honour the Three Lions skipper.
 Kane will also have his Ballon d'Or trophy as fans inside the stadium will be given the chance to mark his achievements.
 77 11 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Kane's special year published at 18:48 GMT 18:48 GMT 
 England v Croatia (19:45 GMT) 
 It has been some year for Harry Kane.
 Scoring goals for fun for Bayern Munich, guiding England to their best-ever finish on foreign soil at a World Cup as they finished third, set to become the Three Lions' record appearance maker and, of course, winning the Ballon d'Or.
 Even though Kane and his England side did not manage to reach the World Cup final, I dare say a more popular winner of the prestigious individual award you could not find.
 Kane beat Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to the award, ending a 25-year wait for an Englishman to be crowned and in so doing, it seems, making the nation very proud.
 Image source, Getty Images

 Kane to set appearance record published at 18:45 GMT 18:45 GMT 
 England v Croatia (19:45 GMT) 
 It's official - Harry Kane will break Peter Shilton’s men’s appearance record of 125 games for England. Kane has scored 91 goals for the Three Lions – 38 more than any other player.
 He is also looking to become the first player since Wayne Rooney in March 2009 to score two or more goals in three appearances in a row.
 Read more about Kane's record here .

 Hello hello... published at 18:33 GMT 18:33 GMT 
 England v Croatia (19:45 GMT) 
 England take on Croatia tonight at Wembley in the Nations League knowing a draw is enough for them to reach the quarter-finals.
 A chance for us all to switch off from domestic football and the drama that it brings? I reckon so.
 So much good stuff to talk about as England captain Harry Kane will play for England for the first time since winning the Ballon d'Or. And, presuming he does play tonight, Kane will celebrate by becoming England's most capped player with this his 126th match.
